newsText: A thousand soldiers answered the call before the first snow. From today each of them, and each heir who carries the family name, wears the ribbon of the First Thousand.

title: Hero of Verdel Ridge
entry: The medal for Verdel Ridge finally came up the line. On Day 3, Lucien "Shadow" Jro was the hundredth man of the Concord, and with him the ridge was theirs. Lucien is gone now, and Cyril after him. The major pinned the medal on {name}: "It belongs to the family. Wear it for both of them."
newsHead: A medal for the Jro family
newsText: On Day 3, Lucien "Shadow" Jro was the hundredth man of the Concord, and Verdel Ridge fell to them. The title never reached him. Lucien and Cyril Jro have both fallen since. Today {name} (@{handle}) carries it for the family: Hero of Verdel Ridge.

text: Today the first trench dogs came up the line. An Airedale, a German shepherd, Jack Russells, collies and a dachshund now sit beside their soldiers on both sides of the wire. Blue, Spot, Socks, Gyp, Ginger, Bess and Scout have already learned where the rations are kept. The men say a trench with a dog in it feels less like a grave.

The Concord holds the line with more men than the Hegemony, and still loses more of them. Half of its new soldiers came up this week and have not learned where to keep their heads. Crates of Hegemony ammunition come up Blackwater Canal every night, so their gunners never stop to count rounds. And the Concord medics cannot reach every stretcher: too many wounded, too few hands. Numbers alone do not hold a trench. Medics, gunners and luck do.

text: Snow began to fall over no man's land in the night. By dawn the wire was white and the craters had a thin crust of ice. The old hands say this is only the start: more snow next week, and real winter after that. Keep your feet dry and your rifle oiled. The cold kills too.
